column1: # Suhalla interiors: residents, merchants, Mind Read, wounded soldiers and travelers.

column3:
I cannot watch someone
in trouble and do
nothing.{page_break}My father says that
instinct is both a gift
and a burden.{end_wait}
I want to help people.\nStanding aside while\nthey suffer feels wrong.{end_wait}

Tolbi rarely thinks of
small places like Suhalla.{page_break}Perhaps that is for the
best. We have enough
trouble of our own.{end_wait}

This is Suhalla's only
store. One shop is
enough for our needs.{page_break}At least, it was before
the storms filled the
streets with strangers.{end_wait}

I wonder if anyone can
reach us through those
storms.{page_break}A traveler would have
to be desperate to cross
the desert now.{end_wait}

We entered the desert
to help build Babi's
lighthouse.{page_break}The storm drove us back.
We cannot reach the
worksite now.{end_wait}
You were blown here\nwhile heading for Babi\nLighthouse, weren't you?{end_now}
The wounded soldiers\nneed quiet until their\nstrength returns.{end_wait}
You expected more shops\nin a village this small?{end_now}

The storms have kept us
busy. More travelers
need food and shelter.{page_break}I am glad we can help,
but I wish they had not
been driven here.{end_wait}
Nothing to do today...{page_break}Perhaps business will\nreturn when the festival\nin Tolbi is over.{end_wait}
Why have the storms\nbecome so fierce? No one\ncan give me an answer.{end_wait}
I feel ill thinking of\nLalivero living under\nTolbi's rule.{end_wait}

My father cannot turn
away anyone in need.{page_break}He gives too much of
himself, but I love him
for it.{end_wait}
Tell me if you need\nanything. I will help\nwhere I can.{end_wait}

From the eastern ridge,
you can see Lalivero
across the Nol River.{page_break}The delta blocks the
way. It is close enough
to see, too far to reach.{end_wait}
Suhalla is only a small\ndesert village. We will\nnever be like Lalivero.{end_wait}
The road to Lalivero is\nnot easy to cross.{page_break}If it were, Suhalla might\nbe forgotten altogether.{end_wait}
A village this small\ncannot support many\nshops.{end_wait}

When the festival ends,
travelers will head south
toward Lalivero.{page_break}If the storms keep them
here, at least they will
spend a little coin.{end_wait}

Anyone caught in a storm
seems to end up here.{page_break}They abandon the road
and take shelter until
the winds have passed.{end_wait}

A cactus steak. The
smell is stronger than
I expected.{page_break}I wonder if it tastes
as good as it looks.{end_wait}

A pot of mulukhiya soup.
The cook says it is
good for the body.{page_break}It smells rich and
comforting.{end_wait}
The wounded are resting.\nKeep your voices low\nand let them sleep.{end_wait}

I cannot believe these
soldiers survived such
terrible wounds.{page_break}They must have been
strong before the storm
found them.{end_wait}

Why were they sent
toward eastern Gondowan?{page_break}Something is wrong.
Please catch up with them
before it is too late.{end_wait}
Where is {actor_name:7}?\nWhat has happened\nto {actor_name:7}?{end_wait}
Who could have brought\nsuch powerful soldiers\nto this condition?{end_wait}

A column of water rose
when the storm caught
them.{page_break}Then the sand fell away.
There was water enough
to fill the whole street.{page_break}No barrel could hold
that much. What power
was it?{end_wait}

{actor_name:7} was close
behind us. She should
still be safe.{page_break}{actor_name:7} must be somewhere
in the desert. Unless
the storm took her...{end_wait}

Stay away from the great
cyclones in the heart
of Suhalla.{page_break}We call them death storms.
Nothing that enters
comes back.{end_wait}

Death storms... There was
a warning about them.
I used to know it.{page_break}Something about eyes...
No, I cannot remember.{end_wait}

Once a death storm takes
you, no one can follow.{page_break}The missing stay lost.
Families wait for years
for those who won't return.{end_wait}

Seek the truth...
Look through the eyes of
wisdom. What was it?{page_break}"When you claim your prize,
a creature of darkness
will guard the way..."{page_break}I know there was more.
The rest has slipped
from my memory.{end_wait}
The storms have brought\nmore customers than\nwe usually see.{end_wait}
The storms may last a\nwhile. Make yourselves\nat home until they pass.{end_wait}
The storms are sending\ntravelers to our door!{page_break}I hope they keep coming.\nIt has been a poor season.{end_wait}
Great storms, send us\nmore customers!{end_wait}
The storms are too fierce\nto reach Babi Lighthouse.\nWe have turned back.{end_wait}
Even if we cannot reach\nthe lighthouse, the work\nwill continue without us.{end_wait}
Should we abandon the\nlighthouse and return\nto Tolbi?{end_wait}

When the cyclone lifted
us from the ground, I
thought we were finished.{page_break}I am grateful to be
alive. Nothing else
matters right now.{end_wait}
I dread leaving town.\nThe storms may take me\nbefore I reach the road.{end_wait}
